katedra: The neoclassical cathedral with its white-columned portico and separate bell tower, the true heart of the city. On the square is the "Stebuklas" (miracle) tile: tradition says you stand on it, turn round three times clockwise and make a wish. Right behind rises the castle hill.
gediminas: What remains of the castle of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania: a red-brick tower on the hill above the Old Town. Inside is a small museum and at the top a terrace with the best view over Vilnius' red rooftops.
valdovu: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania

The Grand Dukes' residence, destroyed in the 19th century and rebuilt in the 2000s at the foot of the hill. Inside are furnished Gothic and Renaissance halls, excavations in the basement and exhibitions on Lithuanian history.
pilies: Pilies Street and the Old Town

The Old Town's main street, running down from Cathedral Square: amber and linen shops, cafés, hidden courtyards and street artists. It continues as Didžioji gatvė to the Town Hall, in the middle of one of Europe's largest Baroque old towns.
univ: University and St John's Bell Tower

One of Eastern Europe's oldest universities (1579): a series of inner courtyards with arcades and frescoes, and St John's Church with its tall white bell tower. From the top you see the whole Old Town.
aurora: Gate of Dawn and St Theresa's Church

The only surviving gate of Vilnius' medieval walls, with a chapel above it, open to the street, where the painting of Our Lady of Mercy is venerated, a pilgrimage site. Next to it is the Baroque St Theresa's Church.
anne: St Anne's and the Bernardine Church
A small red-brick Gothic church with a façade crowded with spires and windows: legend says Napoleon fell in love with it and wanted to take it to Paris. Behind it is the large Bernardine Church.
uzupis: The bohemian quarter across the Vilnia river, which since 1 April 1997 has proclaimed itself a "republic", complete with a Constitution written on plaques in many languages along Paupio gatvė. There are galleries, cafés, the Angel of Užupis statue on the main square and the little Mermaid on the riverbank.
hales: Vilnius' oldest market, in a 1906 iron-framed building: stalls of cheese, meat, vegetables and bread, and small counters with freshly roasted coffee, sandwiches and hot dishes. The right place to taste Lithuanian food without city-centre prices.
kgb: Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights

The museum in the former Soviet KGB headquarters, next to Lukiškės Square: it shows the Soviet occupation and the Lithuanian resistance. The cells and the interrogation room in the basement are the most striking part.
croci: Three large white concrete crosses on a hill east of the Old Town, in Kalnai Park: a free viewpoint, great at sunset, recalling the Franciscan friars said to have been killed there and the Soviet deportations.
